Water, soap and detergent strip stratum corneum lipids and damage keratinocytes directly, with no immune sensitization required. This is the irritant arm of the entry, which is why it targets the toxic-insult node rather than the hapten node the sensitizers use.
Nickel ions released from metal in prolonged skin contact bind self-protein to form the hapten-protein complex this node represents. It is consistently the single most frequent contact allergen.
Fragrance chemicals are a mixture rather than a single molecule, several members of which are haptens; patch testing uses a fragrance mix for that reason.
Preservatives in cosmetics and household products, and the sensitizer behind a documented epidemic of contact allergy after their concentration in leave-on products rose.
A liquid surgical adhesive whose gum-resin constituents can sensitize; reported rarely, so this link records a documented rather than a frequent hapten source.
A surgical skin adhesive increasingly implicated as a sensitizer, notable because the exposure is iatrogenic and occurs on a wound that is already breached.

A second, later encounter with the same adhesive is what recruits primed effector T cells to the skin, which is why staged or repeat surgical procedures carry an order-of-magnitude higher reaction rate than a first exposure. Sensitization and elicitation are separate events, and this link records the second.
The principal sensitizer in permanent hair dye and in black henna tattoos, where the unregulated concentrations make sensitization more likely.
Thiurams and carbamates added during rubber vulcanisation remain in the finished product, which is why gloves intended as protection are themselves a common source of occupational sensitization.
Preservatives and antimicrobials added to cosmetics, cutting fluids and paints, encountered in both occupational and consumer settings.

Not a hapten itself but a property of the encounter. Sensitization is dose- and frequency-dependent, so the same chemical is more likely to prime a T-cell response when met often or at high concentration.
Poison ivy, oak and sumac deliver urushiol, a catechol that penetrates skin and binds protein to form the hapten. Unusually for a contact allergen, it sensitizes a majority of the population.

Phytophotodermatitis needs both halves and is neither allergic nor idiosyncratic: furocoumarins on the skin absorb ultraviolet A and become directly cytotoxic, so the reaction is a phototoxic irritant insult rather than a hapten-driven sensitization.
edges.source: Lime and other psoralen-rich citrus exposure with ultraviolet light

edges.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as two costimulatory and adhesion markers on a monocytic line.
edges.limitations: THP-1 is a monocytic leukemia line, not a dendritic cell, so marker upregulation stands in for antigen-presenting-cell activation rather than demonstrating it. About 15% of outcomes were misclassified in the COLIPA ring trials, with weak allergens and poorly soluble chemicals named as the failure classes. The assay reads a hazard call and carries little potency information, and being cell-only it cannot activate pro-haptens.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step as induced transcriptional change across co-stimulatory, stress and xenobiotic-response programs.
edges.limitations: The readout is a trained signature in the MUTZ-3 dendritic-cell-like myeloid line, so the prediction is model-dependent and the cell is a surrogate rather than a primary dendritic cell. Reported accuracy is tied to the 28-chemical blinded ring-trial set.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Primes an allergen-specific human T-cell response in vitro, which is the step this node asserts, using primary human cells on both sides of the interaction.
edges.limitations: The assay is not regulatory-validated and is low-throughput, and donor-to-donor variability is not yet well defined. It establishes that priming occurs in human cells but cannot establish the whole-organism adverse outcome.

edges.description: Reproduces allergen-driven Langerhans cell maturation together with migration out of the epidermis toward the dermal compartment, which the monolayer dendritic-cell assays cannot show.
edges.limitations: The Langerhans cells are MUTZ-3-derived surrogates rather than primary cells, and the system is a research model without regulatory validation.
edges.source: Full-thickness skin equivalent with MUTZ-3-derived Langerhans cells
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Measures this node's own quantity, Keap1-Nrf2-ARE pathway activation in keratinocytes under hapten exposure, and separates sensitizer-driven from irritant-driven activation on that readout.
edges.limitations: Keratinocytes alone, in monolayer or reconstructed epidermis, so nothing downstream of the sensing step is represented: no Langerhans cells, no dendritic cells, no draining lymph node. The monolayer arms also have no stratum corneum, so they are dosed in medium rather than per unit area of skin surface. These are research systems reading the biology the validated TG 442D methods measure, not those methods themselves.

edges.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as CD86 upregulation on a myeloid line.
edges.limitations: U937 is a myeloid leukemia line, not a dendritic cell, so CD86 upregulation stands in for antigen-presenting-cell activation rather than demonstrating it directly. Between-laboratory reproducibility in the ring study was lower than within-laboratory reproducibility (79% versus 95%), and being cell-only it cannot activate pro-haptens.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as IL-8-promoter luciferase induction in a monocytic reporter line.
edges.limitations: THP-G8 is a monocytic reporter line, not a dendritic cell, so the luciferase readout stands in for antigen-presenting-cell activation rather than demonstrating it directly. The unmodified assay returns an indeterminate call for a chemical that will not dissolve at 20 mg/mL in medium, a documented false-negative route for lipophilic sensitizers with logKow above 3.5; being cell-only it also cannot activate pro-haptens.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Reads the cytoprotective arm of hapten-driven keratinocyte activation as Nrf2-dependent GCLM induction, alongside ATF3 and IL-8 as a separate P2X7-dependent inflammatory readout this entry has no node for.
edges.limitations: The marker genes are a trained signature rather than the Keap1-Nrf2-ARE pathway itself, and the inter-laboratory validation reports a lower specificity (63.0%) than sensitivity (92.6%) against LLNA results. Reported accuracy depends on the LLNA and human comparator datasets used to build it.

edges.description: Reads sensitization hazard and potency from induced expression across a large gene panel in reconstructed epidermis, rather than from a single pathway readout.
edges.limitations: The panel is a trained signature over many genes rather than a mechanistic readout of one step, so which genes drive a given call is not individually interpretable from the model record alone. Reported predictivity figures come from the ring-study and 150-chemical test sets used to validate it.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Reads the inflammasome-dependent danger-signalling arm of keratinocyte activation as secreted IL-18 and IL-1beta from a topically dosed tissue construct under perfusion, rather than from a monolayer.
edges.limitations: This is a proof-of-concept study with one sensitizer (cinnamaldehyde) and no irritant or non-sensitizer comparator, so sensitizer specificity of the cytokine panel is not established from this report alone.
edges.source: Reconstructed human skin organ-on-chip with neopapillae (RhS-NP)

edges.description: Reads dendritic-cell-surrogate activation (CD83 and CD86 upregulation on MUTZ-3) occurring when immune cells flow past an endothelialised skin construct topically exposed to a sensitizer, adding circulation and a vascular interface that static monolayer and reconstructed-tissue assays lack.
edges.limitations: This is a proof-of-concept demonstration with one sensitizer and no comparator irritant or non-sensitizer, so specificity is not established from this report alone. MUTZ-3 is a dendritic-cell-like line rather than a primary dendritic cell.
edges.source: Endothelialised skin-on-chip with flowing immune cells (MMA-6MWP)
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Removes Langerhans cells and shows contact hypersensitivity is amplified rather than abolished, so Langerhans cells are dispensable for priming and act to restrain it. This revises the antigen-presenting-cell assumption this node inherits.
edges.limitations: Mouse genetic ablation; the dendritic-cell subset that primes the response in the absence of Langerhans cells is not identified, in this work or since, and the human priming antigen-presenting cell remains unresolved.
edges.target: Skin innate immune activation during sensitization

edges.description: Shows that loss of NALP3 or ASC impairs the response to contact sensitizers, establishing the caspase-1-dependent IL-1beta and IL-18 processing this node asserts as a required part of the sensitization response rather than an incidental accompaniment of it.
edges.limitations: Mouse knockouts; the companion human evidence is in keratinocytes in vitro rather than in human skin.
edges.source: NALP3- and ASC-deficient contact hypersensitivity mouse

edges.description: Measures the regulatory arm whose failure this node asserts, rather than reproducing that failure. Hapten immunization of wild-type mice induces a CD4+CD25+ regulatory T-cell population that suppresses hapten-reactive CD8+ effectors in a hapten-specific manner, so the model shows the suppression intact and characterizes the population whose loss the node records.
edges.limitations: Mouse contact hypersensitivity; the human counterpart evidence for hapten tolerance is in vitro nickel-responsiveness in healthy donors rather than in vivo.
edges.source: DNFB contact hypersensitivity regulatory T-cell model
edges.target: Breakdown of regulatory T-cell-mediated hapten tolerance

edges.description: Reads draining-lymph-node T-cell proliferation after dermal exposure, so it integrates penetration, metabolism, antigen-presenting-cell migration and clonal expansion in one whole-organism readout.
edges.limitations: Mouse; it misses metal sensitizers, with nickel sulfate hexahydrate recorded as a false negative, which is consistent with metals initiating through human TLR4 rather than covalent binding. Potency estimates are also vehicle-dependent.

edges.description: The scored endpoint is the challenge-patch reaction in an animal already induced with the test chemical, so what the assay reads is the elicitation response to re-exposure rather than the priming that produced it. Priming is inferred from the presence of that reaction.
edges.limitations: Guinea pig rather than human, and the endpoint is a visually graded skin reaction rather than an antigen-specific cellular measurement. The adjuvant and intradermal induction are more aggressive than any topical human exposure, which is what makes this the sensitive member of the pair and also what makes a positive result an upper bound on potency. Chlorhexidine is negative in this test, and the guinea pig methods as a class have recorded false positives for vanillin and sulfanilic acid and a false negative for abietic acid.

edges.description: Reads the same challenge-patch reaction as the maximization test, under a milder induction regimen. Fidelity is graded LOW because the method returns negative results for chemicals that are strong sensitizers in the parallel test, so a negative here does not constrain whether the mechanism occurred.
edges.limitations: Guinea pig, and the readout is a visually graded skin reaction. Eugenol and mercaptobenzothiazole are negative in this test while scoring as strong sensitizers in the maximization test under identical conditions, and higher induction concentrations are needed before allergenicity shows at all. For some allergens the protocol is not sensitive enough to demonstrate the potential, so negative results carry little weight.

nodes.description: A pre-hapten is a contact allergen that is not itself protein-reactive but is converted to a reactive electrophile by abiotic, nonenzymatic oxidation that can occur independently of the skin (on air exposure, for example). nodes.description: A reactive small chemical forms a covalent bond with a skin protein, generating the hapten-protein adduct that downstream innate and adaptive responses recognize. This is the molecular initiating event of skin sensitization and is rate-limiting for sensitizer potency. The step itself is well established, but its molecular target in skin is not: the available evidence is in chemico and in vitro, using synthetic peptides, albumin in solution and cultured human cells, and the assays of this field measure bulk cysteine-peptide depletion as a surrogate. Which specific epidermal protein has to be modified for the downstream steps to follow remains unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Tracking human contact allergens: from mass spectrometric identification of peptide-bound reactive small chemicals to chemical-specific naive human T-cell priming.
evidence.snippet: Modification of proteins by reactive small chemicals is a key step in the activation of chemical-specific T cells in allergic contact dermatitis (ACD).

evidence.snippet: The reaction of sensitizing molecules with skin proteins is the molecular initiating event and appears to be rate-limiting, as chemical reactivity strongly correlates with sensitizer potency.

evidence.snippet: The analysis of the Cys-adducts was already sufficient; additional analysis of Lys-adducts did not improve the predictivity.

evidence.snippet: With these two compounds excluded, sensitization potency is well correlated with the experimental rate constants for the DNXB compounds (X = SO3(-), I, Br, Cl) together with 2,4-dichloro-1-nitrobenzene and 1,3,4,5-tetrachloro-2,6-dicyanobenzene. The regression equation is pEC3 = 0.88 log k + 4.03, R(2) = 0.966.

Because the RhE model retains a stratified stratum corneum and metabolic competence, it can be dosed topically and can activate lipophilic chemicals and pre-/pro-haptens that monolayer cell-line assays miss.

nodes.description: Keratinocytes read the hapten as an electrophile and mount a Keap1-Nrf2-ARE antioxidant-response programme: Nrf2 protein accumulates, translocates to the nucleus, and activates its transcriptional targets. This is the electrophile-sensing arm of the sensitization-phase keratinocyte step corresponding to AOP 40 Key Event 826 (Activation, Keratinocytes), and the cause is the chemistry of the hapten rather than barrier injury: the response separates a sensitizer from an irritant at non-toxic concentrations, which is the biology the OECD TG 442D methods measure. It is curated apart from the inflammasome danger-signalling arm of the same Key Event, which runs through IL-1 family cytokines and carries its own node, because the two are read by different models.

evidence.snippet: Irritant contact dermatitis is a result of activated innate immune response to various external stimuli and consists of complex interplay which involves skin barrier disruption, cellular changes, and release of proinflammatory mediators.

nodes.description: The hapten acts as a danger signal in keratinocytes: the NLRP3 and ASC inflammasome assembles and activates caspase-1, which processes pro-IL-1beta and pro-IL-18 to their mature forms and releases them. This is the danger-signalling arm of the sensitization-phase keratinocyte step corresponding to AOP 40 Key Event 826, running in parallel with Keap1-Nrf2-ARE electrophile sensing rather than downstream of it, and it supplies the proinflammatory cytokines the innate and adaptive steps below require. Like the sensing arm it is driven by the hapten and not by barrier disruption, which is what separates it from the irritant arm's keratinocyte node.

animal_models.description: Shows that loss of NALP3 or ASC impairs the response to contact sensitizers, establishing the caspase-1-dependent IL-1beta and IL-18 processing this node asserts as a required part of the sensitization response rather than an incidental accompaniment of it.
animal_models.name: NALP3- and ASC-deficient contact hypersensitivity mouse

evidence.reference_title: Activation of the IL-1beta-processing inflammasome is involved in contact hypersensitivity.
evidence.snippet: We show here that key components of the inflammasome are present in human keratinocytes and that CS like trinitro-chlorobenzene induce caspase-1/ASC dependent IL-1beta and IL-18 processing and secretion.

evidence.reference_title: Inflammasome activation in delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions.
evidence.snippet: The study documents a regulatory effect of innate immunity in a T-cell-mediated delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction.

experimental_models.description: Reads the inflammasome-dependent danger-signalling arm of keratinocyte activation as secreted IL-18 and IL-1beta from a topically dosed tissue construct under perfusion, rather than from a monolayer.
experimental_models.name: Reconstructed human skin organ-on-chip with neopapillae (RhS-NP)

nodes.description: A pro-hapten is a contact allergen that is not itself protein-reactive but requires enzymatic metabolism in skin, chiefly by cytochrome P450 and NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) in keratinocytes, to become a reactive electrophile. This route sits upstream of the covalent-binding step rather than around it, so the protein-reactive species a sensitized person actually generates can differ from the parent chemical applied to the skin.
nodes.id: Keratinocyte pro-hapten bioactivation to a reactive electrophile

evidence.reference_title: Cross talk between keratinocytes and dendritic cells: impact on the prediction of sensitization.
evidence.snippet: Under coculture conditions, the prohaptens eugenol, 2-methoxy-4-methylphenol, and benzo ... pyrene induced a significantly higher upregulation of CD86 expression on THP-1.

evidence.reference_title: Finding the optimal patch test material and test concentration to detect contact allergy to geraniol.
evidence.snippet: Reactions to pure geraniol in patients not reacting to oxidized geraniol indicated metabolic activation of geraniol.

nodes.description: A BAC transgenic mouse with constitutive, durable absence of epidermal Langerhans cells and otherwise intact immunity, used to test whether Langerhans cells are required to prime contact hypersensitivity.
Contact with lime juice or peel followed by ultraviolet exposure can trigger phytophotodermatitis, a phototoxic contact reaction that may be mistaken for allergic dermatitis.
nodes.id: Lime and other psoralen-rich citrus exposure with ultraviolet light

evidence.reference_title: Mojito-Induced Phytophotodermatitis: A Case of Lime-Triggered Skin Reaction.
evidence.snippet: Lime-induced phytophotodermatitis, sometimes called "lime disease" or "margarita photodermatitis," is one of the most common forms, caused by furocoumarins in lime juice or peel.

nodes.description: Exposure to Mastisol liquid adhesive used for wound closure is a reported trigger of allergic contact dermatitis after surgical procedures.

evidence.reference_title: Allergic Contact Dermatitis to Mastisol Adhesive Used for Skin Closure in Orthopedic Surgery: A Case Report.
evidence.snippet: We report on a rare case of allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) from Mastisol liquid adhesive.

nodes.description: Activated effector and resident memory T cells amplify IFNg-, IL-17A-, IL-1beta-, and chemokine-rich inflammatory programs, with predominant type 1 and type 3 effector responses and lesser type 2 contributions.
nodes.id: Mixed type 1 and type 3 cytokine and chemokine amplification

evidence.reference_title: CD100 boosts the inflammatory response in the challenge phase of allergic contact dermatitis in mice.
evidence.snippet: We show that loss of CD100 results in a reduced inflammatory response to DNFB with impaired production of IFNγ, IL-17A, CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCL5, and IL-1β and decreased recruitment of neutrophils to the epidermis.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Allergic Patch Test Reactions in Non‐Atopic Patients: A Comparative Study Across Multiple Allergens
evidence.snippet: All allergens exhibited mixed effector immune responses, mainly type 1 and 3 immunity, and, to a lesser extent, type 2 immunity.

nodes.description: The regulatory animal method (OECD TG 429, 442A, 442B) that reads sensitization as proliferation of T cells in the lymph node draining the site of dermal exposure.
Inflammasome-component knockouts exposed to contact sensitizers, used to test whether keratinocyte inflammasome signaling is required for the innate arm of contact hypersensitivity.
nodes.id: NALP3- and ASC-deficient contact hypersensitivity mouse

nodes.description: Exposure to nickel-containing jewelry, tools, and occupational metal sources is a common environmental trigger of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.reference_title: Advancing the understanding of allergic contact dermatitis: from pathophysiology to novel therapeutic approaches

nodes.description: Exposure to para-phenylenediamine, particularly in hair dyes and related products, is a common environmental trigger of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.reference_title: Advancing the understanding of allergic contact dermatitis: from pathophysiology to novel therapeutic approaches
evidence.snippet: Metals, especially nickel, fragrance mix, isothiazolinones, and para-phenylenediamine, are the most commonly positive allergens in patients patch tested for suspected ACD.

evidence.reference_title: Eyelid Contact Dermatitis: 25-Year Single-Center Retrospective Study.
evidence.snippet: Background/Objectives: Eyelid dermatitis is an inflammatory disease affecting the palpebral skin characterized by itching, edema, and scaling of the periorbital area.

nodes.description: Upon renewed hapten exposure, primed effector T cells re-enter skin and initiate the elicitation phase of allergic contact dermatitis.

animal_models.description: The scored endpoint is the challenge-patch reaction in an animal already induced with the test chemical, so what the assay reads is the elicitation response to re-exposure rather than the priming that produced it. Priming is inferred from the presence of that reaction.
animal_models.name: Guinea pig maximization test

animal_models.description: Reads the same challenge-patch reaction as the maximization test, under a milder induction regimen. Fidelity is graded LOW because the method returns negative results for chemicals that are strong sensitizers in the parallel test, so a negative here does not constrain whether the mechanism occurred.
animal_models.name: Buehler occluded patch test

evidence.reference_title: Effector and regulatory mechanisms in allergic contact dermatitis.
evidence.snippet: Allergic contact dermatitis, also referred to as contact hypersensitivity, is mediated by CD8+ T cells, which are primed in lymphoid organs during the sensitization phase and are recruited in the skin upon re-exposure to the hapten.

nodes.description: A next-generation skin-on-chip combining a stratified, differentiated epidermis on a fibroblast-populated hydrogel containing dermal-papilla spheroids (neopapillae), cultured air-exposed under dynamic flow and dosed topically with a sensitizer.
nodes.id: Reconstructed human skin organ-on-chip with neopapillae (RhS-NP)

evidence.reference_title: Proof-of-Concept Organ-on-Chip Study: Topical Cinnamaldehyde Exposure of Reconstructed Human Skin with Integrated Neopapillae Cultured under Dynamic Flow.
evidence.snippet: This study demonstrates the robustness and feasibility of complex next generation skin models for investigating skin immunotoxicity.

nodes.description: Repeated contact and higher local concentrations of potential allergens increase the probability of sensitization and later allergic flares.

evidence.reference_title: Identifying the causes of contact dermatitis.
evidence.snippet: Frequent exposure and high concentrations of potential allergens increase the risk of sensitisation.

nodes.description: Epidermal resident memory CD8-positive T cells are activated in allergen-experienced skin and intensify local flare responses.

evidence.reference_title: CD100 boosts the inflammatory response in the challenge phase of allergic contact dermatitis in mice.
evidence.snippet: BACKGROUND: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) is an inflammatory disease with a complex pathophysiology in which epidermal-resident memory CD8+ T (TRM ) cells play a key role.

nodes.description: Exposure to rubber accelerators in gloves, footwear, and occupational materials is a common environmental trigger of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.reference_title: Identifying the causes of contact dermatitis.
evidence.snippet: Nickel, fragrances, rubber accelerators and biocides are the most common sensitisers in ACD.

nodes.description: A reconstructed human epidermis (Episkin) gene-expression assay that quantifies sensitization hazard and potency from a large transcriptional panel, the same stratum-corneum-intact, metabolically competent format EpiSensA also uses.

evidence.reference_title: SENS-IS, a 3D reconstituted epidermis based model for quantifying chemical sensitization potency: Reproducibility and predictivity results from an inter-laboratory study.
evidence.snippet: data analysis confirmed the excellent capacity of the SENS-IS assay for predicting both hazard and potency characteristics, confirming that this assay should be considered as a serious alternative to the available in vivo sensitization tests.

nodes.description: Early innate immune signaling in allergen-exposed skin shapes the sensitization phase and supports subsequent adaptive immune priming.

animal_models.name: Langerin-DTA Langerhans-cell-deficient mouse

evidence.reference_title: Effector and regulatory mechanisms in allergic contact dermatitis.
evidence.snippet: Recent advances in the pathophysiology of ACD have demonstrated the important role of skin innate immunity in the sensitization process

experimental_models.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as two costimulatory and adhesion markers on a monocytic line.
experimental_models.name: Human Cell Line Activation Test (h-CLAT)

experimental_models.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step as induced transcriptional change across co-stimulatory, stress and xenobiotic-response programs.
experimental_models.name: GARDskin

experimental_models.description: Reproduces allergen-driven Langerhans cell maturation together with migration out of the epidermis toward the dermal compartment, which the monolayer dendritic-cell assays cannot show.
experimental_models.name: Full-thickness skin equivalent with MUTZ-3-derived Langerhans cells

experimental_models.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as CD86 upregulation on a myeloid line.
experimental_models.name: U-SENS (Myeloid U937 Skin Sensitization Test)

experimental_models.description: Reads the dendritic-cell activation step of sensitization as IL-8-promoter luciferase induction in a monocytic reporter line.
experimental_models.name: IL-8 Luc assay

experimental_models.description: Reads sensitization hazard and potency from induced expression across a large gene panel in reconstructed epidermis, rather than from a single pathway readout.
experimental_models.name: SENS-IS

experimental_models.description: Reads dendritic-cell-surrogate activation (CD83 and CD86 upregulation on MUTZ-3) occurring when immune cells flow past an endothelialised skin construct topically exposed to a sensitizer, adding circulation and a vascular interface that static monolayer and reconstructed-tissue assays lack.
experimental_models.name: Endothelialised skin-on-chip with flowing immune cells (MMA-6MWP)

nodes.description: Exposure to Toxicodendron plants such as poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac is a common environmental trigger of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.reference_title: Topical pimecrolimus in the treatment of human allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.reference_title: CD1a on Langerhans cells controls inflammatory skin disease.
evidence.snippet: Among various urushiol congeners, we identified diunsaturated pentadecylcatechol (C15:2) as the dominant antigen for CD1a-restricted T cells.

nodes.description: An OECD TG 442E method that reads sensitizer-induced activation of a dendritic-cell surrogate as CD86 surface expression on the U937 human myeloid cell line, measured by flow cytometry.

evidence.reference_title: The Myeloid U937 Skin Sensitization Test (U-SENS) addresses the activation of dendritic cell event in the adverse outcome pathway for skin sensitization.
evidence.snippet: U-SENS™ showed 79% specificity, 90% sensitivity and 88% accuracy.

nodes.description: Repetitive wet work and exposure to soaps and detergents are common environmental drivers of irritant contact dermatitis, especially on the hands.

evidence.reference_title: Identifying the causes of contact dermatitis.
